item.title: Oct. 7 Commemoration — Tue Oct 6, 6:00 PM
item.description:
“We Will Always Remember” An Oct. 7th Commemoration Event Tuesday, Oct. 6 at 7:00 p.m. at Congregation Beth Ami Join us as we remember the victims of the Hamas terrorist attacks carried out on Oct. 7, 2023. The massacre began at approximately 6:30 am in Israel, so our hearts will be with them, as we gather near the time that the terrible events unfolded there. This will be a multi-community gathering of remembering. Remembering those who lost their lives. Remembering those who risked their lives to save others. Remembering not to lose hope - and to stand as one, together. There will be a short memorial service, as well as selected readings and music. Come stand with the Jewish community as we remember together. RSVP required - office@bethamisr.org or (707) 360- 3000
Source: Congregation Beth Ami

item.title: Petaluma Film Festival Presents: Brian w/ producer in conversation — Wed Oct 7, 6:00 PM — Carole L. Ellis Hall
item.description:
Brian \(Ben Wang\), is a smart, quirky, and somewhat maladjusted high school student who struggles with anxiety and mental health issues. With the help of his therapist \(William H. Macy\) and the new kid at school, Justin \(Joshua Colley\), he decides to launch a high-stakes campaign for class president to win over his high school teacher crush. Actor-turned-director Will Ropp delivers a funny and heartfelt dark comedy that explores teen isolation, neurodivergence, and the messy road to self-acceptance in an original, sensitive, and nuanced way. The film debuted to rave reviews at the 2026 SXSW Film Festival and is co-presented by the 2026 Mill Valley Film Festival. Producer Casey Hanley will participate in an onstage interview at 6pm and answer questions following the 7pm screening.
The Petaluma Film Alliance is proud to partner with the 49th Mill Valley Film Festival to bring you this special educational screening. Visit mvff.com for the complete line-up of films screening October

item.title: Work In Progress - Robert Reich new Movie — Wed Oct 7, 6:00 PM — Sebastiani Theatre
item.description:
“The Work in Progress” takes viewers on a tour of the American spirit at a time of deep division. Guided by UC Berkeley emeritus scholar Robert Reich, the documentary finds tension and doubt everywhere — but also signs of hope.Inspired by Robert Reich's curiosity and humanity, it is a testament to the power of listening, civic engagement, and the belief that our shared future is still ours to shape. Th film begins with Professor Reich asking "What do we owe each other?" What follows is a journey to find out.
A Q&A with producers Heather Kinlaw Lofthouse, a UC Berkeley graduate, and Elliot Kirschner will follow the film
The film is a timely and thought-provoking addition to Reich's catalogue of writing, film, media appearances and other public commentary. Perhaps it's no surprise that it emerges from the culture of UC Berkeley.
